title: Integrating morphological and molecular perspectives on foraging tactic constancy in a nectar-robbing bumble bee
orientation_basis: smaller Bombus body size is associated with greater use of secondary nectar robbing rather than legitimate foraging; legitimate access to long-spurred Linaria requires greater reach/handling ability
evidence_basis: Primary article reports legitimate foragers larger, secondary robbers smaller and switchers intermediate; body size is quantitatively associated with tactic, and the discussion explicitly links morphology to legitimate access into the long floral spur.
